fatal_errors: The proposed RHEAs contain no solid-lubricant or tribofilm-forming architecture and therefore do not address self-lubrication.
The hypothesis omits the target CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite and the controlled variation of Mo content.

Its nanoprecipitation, short-range-order, and cross-slip mechanisms do not reconstruct the target solid-solution/σ-phase strengthening and temperature-dependent MoS2, Ag, oxide, and silver-molybdate lubrication mechanisms.
No friction or wear measurements are proposed, so the central wide-temperature tribological claim cannot be tested.
The cited evidence concerns mechanical strength and thermal stability of RHEAs rather than dry-sliding self-lubrication from room temperature to 800 °C.
explanation: The response addresses high-temperature structural strength but largely substitutes a generic RHEA strength–ductility hypothesis for the requested self-lubricating material. It fails to identify the Mo-varied CoCrFeNi-based composite containing Ni-coated MoS2, Ag, and Cr2O3, and it does not reproduce SPS processing or ball-on-disk conditions. The key target mechanism is a combination of Mo-induced lattice distortion and σ-phase strengthening with low-temperature MoS2/Ag lubrication and high-temperature oxide/silver-molybdate glaze formation. None of these tribological mediators appears in the generated hypothesis. Although the cited papers reasonably support some general RHEA mechanical-property claims, they provide no valid evidence for stable friction or wear performance. The proposed falsification experiment measures only mechanical and microstructural properties and therefore cannot discriminate whether the material is self-lubricating.
